name: Ronald Adonis
caption: LOL's own Chancellor and majority shareholder, described in the fed's own FAQ as a committed wrestling fan who founded the promotion and lent his birthplace's name to its secondary title.

tenures.source: The fed's own Frequently Asked Questions (21 July 1998): "The Chancellor (ie supremo) of the LOL; a comitted wrestling fan, he founded the LOL and still owns a majority shareholding." Still in the office on the fed's own 17 June 1999 broadcast, on which he holds up the World Tag Teem title in a Chancellorial announcement, and on its 20 June 1999 broadcast, on which he is credited with the same ruling.

name: Richard Chopper
caption: LOL's senior ring announcer, per the fed's own FAQ.

tenures.source: The fed's own Frequently Asked Questions (21 July 1998): "LOL's senior ring announcer; nothing special about him. Yet." Still calling matches and announcing decisions throughout the fed's 1999 return, per every broadcast now served.

name: Zarg the Unmercible
caption: An alien warlord bent on world domination, per the fed's own FAQ, which reassures readers not to worry about him too much.

tenures.source: The fed's own Frequently Asked Questions (21 July 1998): "An alien warlord bent on world domination. I shouldn't worry about him too much, though."

name: Van Halent
caption: A glam-rock LOL Galactic Champion, mobbed by adoring fans wherever he goes, who won the belt at the fed's own 1998 season finale and carried it through its 1999 return.

tenures.source: Billed the reigning LOL Galactic Champion throughout the fed's 1998-99 record, per the fed's own 16 April, 25 April and 6 June 1999 broadcasts and its own recap of the SantaSlam '98 finale where he won the title.

name: G.I. Slow
caption: A military-parody LOL wrestler, billed Orange Grove Texas Champion entering the fed's 1999 return before losing the title, who later teamed with Sergeant Slumber as the Real American Zeroes to win the fed's first World Tag Teem title.

tenures.source: Billed the LOL Orange Grove Texas Champion on the fed's own 16 April 1999 broadcast; lost the title on 6 June 1999 and won the World Tag Teem title with Sergeant Slumber on 3 June 1999, per the fed's own broadcasts.

name: Sergeant Slumber
caption: A narcoleptic military-parody LOL wrestler, half of the tag team the Real American Zeroes alongside G.I. Slow, with whom he won the fed's first World Tag Teem title.

tenures.source: Billed half of the Real American Zeroes, the fed's first World Tag Teem Champions, on the fed's own 3 June 1999 broadcast.

name: "The Loose Screw" Dmitri Damian Maku Stalin
caption: A wild-eyed LOL wrestler billed from Tbilisi, Georgia, who won the Orange Grove Texas title on the fed's 6 June 1999 broadcast and successfully defended it two weeks later.

tenures.source: Won the LOL Orange Grove Texas title on the fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast and defended it on the fed's own 20 June 1999 broadcast.

name: "The Simple Man" Ken E. Cheznee
caption: A LOL wrestler who challenged Van Halent for the Galactic title on the fed's 6 June 1999 broadcast, losing by disqualification after outside interference rather than by his own hand.

tenures.source: Challenged Van Halent for the LOL Galactic title on the fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast, losing by disqualification after interference from a third wrestler.

name: Bubbolicious Bob
caption: A recurring LOL wrestler who paired with Van Halent to win the World Tag Teem title on the fed's 14 June 1999 broadcast, days before the pairing broke up and the title was held up.

tenures.source: Billed a recurring LOL wrestler across the fed's 1999 broadcasts; won the World Tag Teem title paired with Van Halent on the fed's own 14 June 1999 broadcast.

name: "The Mexican Dream" Dusty Sanchez
caption: A LOL wrestler who challenged G.I. Slow for the Orange Grove Texas title on the fed's 25 April 1999 broadcast, losing by pinfall.

tenures.source: Challenged G.I. Slow for the LOL Orange Grove Texas title on the fed's own 25 April 1999 broadcast, losing by pinfall.

name: "Red Hot" Cobra Commander
caption: A G.I. Joe-parody LOL wrestler, accompanied by Destro, who challenged Van Halent for the Galactic title on the fed's 25 April 1999 broadcast, losing by pinfall.

tenures.source: Challenged Van Halent for the LOL Galactic title on the fed's own 25 April 1999 broadcast, losing by pinfall after his own ally's interference backfired.

name: Clint Earl Nicholson
caption: Half of the LOL tag team the Nominees, who lost a title-unification match to the Real American Zeroes on the fed's 3 June 1999 broadcast after a controversial belt theft angle.

tenures.source: Half of the Nominees, who made off with the World Tag Teem title belts after an elimination tournament's own contested finish, then lost a deciding title match to the Real American Zeroes, on the fed's own 3 June 1999 broadcast.

name: Sean Lee Hanks
caption: Half of the LOL tag team the Nominees, who lost a title-unification match to the Real American Zeroes on the fed's 3 June 1999 broadcast after a controversial belt theft angle.

tenures.source: Half of the Nominees, who made off with the World Tag Teem title belts after an elimination tournament's own contested finish, then lost a deciding title match to the Real American Zeroes, on the fed's own 3 June 1999 broadcast.

name: The Dodo
caption: The LOL Galactic Champion before Van Halent won the title from him at the fed's own SantaSlam '98 season finale, per the fed's own later recap; no document of his own reign survives in the record.

tenures.source: Named in the fed's own 4 April 1999 reopening announcement as one of the fed's earlier 1998-era stars, and in its own 16 April 1999 broadcast recap as the Galactic Champion Van Halent dethroned at SantaSlam '98.
